2016 Man of the Year: American Men

This was years and years ago.

I woke up in sheets of yellow, after a long stint of drug abuse. No idea how long it had been, maybe about a week. The sheets were actually white but my sweat was yellow due to my liver being challenged.

I get up and walk to the bathroom and the first thing I do is look in the mirror. A common action. But what looked back at me was not a usual site. I was a skeleton. A corpse. My eyes were sunk in and my cheeks were like knives. I was dead. I felt dead and I looked dead. A ghost stared back at me.

That was it for me.

I've had my set backs but since then I've tried to make the best of what I call life. In no way will I ever be back there. Fuck being a living ghost.
Care to share your moment of clarity?

This is sort of a two-parter. My 'moment' was in two halves, separated by a decent bit of time.

I had moved to NYC a few years back, and become an authority figure in this kid's life over the course of my time there. His bio-dad was missing in action, and his stepdad was kindof a piece of shit. I really took pride in being somebody he could look up to, trust, and maybe hope to be like, just a little bit. He moved in with me to get out of his toxic situation at home, and then moved out to live with his boyfriend in another town. Somewhat abruptly, he got very distant, and more or less stopped talking to me altogether. He'd come up with his boyfriend sometimes to visit, but he didn't interact with me much.

My alcoholism was bad, but as my relationship with my boyfriend failed harder, I had started to drink less for the 'drunk' but more so that my brain would be "hangover altered" while I was sober, because that's what I was doing to get through. That takes a lot of alcohol.

One night, he was up, another friend was visiting from out of town, and I was celebrating all the company. I got way too drunk, slurring, blurry-eyed and nihilistic. I smashed the kid's glasses, without even realizing I'd thrashed on them. And at some point, while my boyfriend and out-of-town visitor tried to calm me down, I realized that I hadn't seen the kid or his boyfriend in awhile. I asked where they were, and I was told they went home. At three in the morning, they packed up their shit, walked a mile and a half in the cold to their car, and drove three hours home, just to get away from me because I was too drunk and everything was too damaging. That was the moment that I finally comprehended and accepted the magnitude of what I had become, and how pathetic of a creature I was, regardless of whether my paycheck was covering the bills or whether I had the house generally in order.

That was the first half. Because I sobered up the next day, apologized to everyone for my behavior, and kept drinking. The second half of that moment came maybe six months, or a year after that.

The kid I talked about before--he messaged me, sorta-kinda out of nowhere. He told me that he had blocked me out of his life and really tried to buck off any positive feelings he still had for me, because my drinking was just too painful to watch and he couldn't be close to me. But, he wanted to try again, because there was just this void in his life where a positive male figure ought to be, and he didn't feel like things were good for him. The night after that, I got online with him, we trolled 4chan together, and I got fairly tipsy. I woke up the following morning, and said to myself, "Ok, you're not going to put him through that again."

And I didn't. I spent a year sober in order to make sure that, no matter how I fucked up, I didn't start hurting myself like that again. It's been about another year since then, and I've reintroduced alcohol to my life carefully, with a lot of input from those close to me, and most notably, in moderation.

It's strange to reflect on now and really say it, but honestly, I don't know if I could bring myself to avoid the trap of alcoholism altogether, if I were elevated to the level of The Fates and given the chance to pluck at my own life-string. It was a crucible, and it took me far too long to pull myself out of it, but I certainly did. And I don't think I could really be the quality of man I am today if I didn't.
